titleStmt.title: Measurement of cache-related preemption delay for spacecraft computers

analytic.title: Measurement of cache-related preemption delay for spacecraft computers

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In order to guarantee task schedulability in realtime embedded systems, analysis on cache and cache behavior at task preemption is required because cache misses cause unpredictable delays in task execution time. Nevertheless, studies on cache behavior and its effects in preemptive multitasking systems have been conducted mainly with simulation and analytic methods, which may induce pessimistic scheduling policy. In this paper, we propose a measurement framework to diagnose the cache-related preemption delay (CRPD) on LEON3 SPARC V8 processor to understand its effect with execution time analysis. The experimental results from several benchmark program execution on the framework show that the time delay and penalty for cache operations are not constant. We were able to identify that each software has a unique degree of cache susceptibility with regard to CRPD. We conclude that this experiment data can be used to prevent real-time tasks from missing the deadline, which is not tolerable in real-time constraints of spacecraft computers, by applying it on real-time scheduling. The results may be useful to the susceptibility analysis of real-time embedded software. The measured CRPD on a specified real target processor can be used to assess the schedulability of task sets to bound WCET on task preemption condition.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Cache brings high CPU performance. But cache system operates in the real-time embedded systems with a highly unpredictable manner at run-time. Cache misses cause unpredictable effects on response time behavior on a task known as CRPD (Cache-Related Preemption Delay). It is difficult to evaluate the schedulability unless the pessimistic margin is involved with regard to CRPD. Cache behavior in multitasking and preemptive environments is unpredictable, so predicting occurrence and impacts of the cache hit and miss at run-time is necessary to ensure the schedulability of a task.

An execution time measurement framework for SPARC V8 LEON3 VHDL development board is developed to measure the impact caused by cache flush on preemption. Through this framework, it is possible to specifically address the impact of CRPD by inter-task contention on the LEON3 processor architecture. A number of certain benchmark software are executed on the framework. From the results of these benchmark execution, we explore the cache interference on task preemption and present a way to reflect its effect on the response time analysis.

div.head: II. DESIGN OF THE EXECUTION TIME MEASUREMENT FRAMEWORK
div.p: We choose a LEON3-IP core FPGA evaluation system, which runs GRLIB LEON3-IP core [1], as test hardware platform in this study because LEON3 is one of the prominent processors for space application as the main processor and for the payload controller. To simplify the complexity of the test environment, we use a Bare C compiler for SPARC instead of an RTOS (e.g. VxWorks or RTEMS).

GRLIB provides L3STAT (LEON3 Statistics Unit) which is used to count processor events in the LEON3 processor and on the AHB bus, in order to aggregate performance statistics for various software applications [1]. We modify the design of the L3STAT to support a larger number of counters and improve the functionality so that it can effectively measure cache events and execution time through various control function. We name it as Processor Cache Report Register (PCRR).
A number of benchmarks are selected among those used in related studies [2], [3].

• DES [4], Dhrystone, MiBench 1.0 -basicmath, bitcount, dijkstra [5], [6], RungeKutta [7], Stanford[8], and Whetstone[9] We consider two experimental environments to distinguish cache behavior and its impacts to execution time between an ambient condition of without task preemption (-intrinsic environment) and preemption condition with cache flush (extrinsic environment).

div.head: III. EXPERIMENT RESULTS AND ANALYSIS
div.p: This section presents the results of experiments which are described above section. Table I shows the results of benchmarks execution under the controlled conditions and operations. The framework also gathers total execution clock cycle during software execution and the execution time (sec) is calculated from (total clock cycle / 50 MHz).

Table II shows shows the analysis results which presents the correlation between cache flushing overhead and its impact to the susceptibility of each benchmark software. We observe that each of benchmarks has unique behavior when exterior disturbance as cache flushing is applied. The benchmarks that carry frequent cache misses are more susceptible to cache flush event, and have bigger overhead per cache flush event to recover the cache contents to the previous state before task preemption happens. We interpret it as a task whose cache misses interval is relatively short has more vigorous use of cache, and high chances to extensively use more cache area than others. The value of the last column of Table II, Severity of CRPD, may provide crucial criterion which explains the unique behavior and criticality of task on task preemption event. According to the analysis, the basicmath is more susceptible cache behavior model in code implementation than Dhrystone, which means it consumes more CPU cycles to recover the evicted cache blocks than the other cases which have lower severity.

div.head: IV. CONCLUSIONS AND FUTURE WORK
div.p: In this paper, an execution time measurement framework for real-time embedded systems on a target of LEON3 SPARC V8 processor board has been presented. This framework is specialized in measuring CRPD on real hardware target platforms and the measured CRPD data can be utilized in response time analysis to reflect the actual impact of cache interference at task preemption. This observation to cache flushing effect on preemption can be used to estimate the temporal behavior of a task which runs with other multiple tasks because the variation of the measured CRPD is relatively small according to the results of the experiment with the presented framework.

In future, we plan to enhance the framework to be operable with a real-time operating system like RTEMS [10] with multiple contentions between real-time task set which reflects actual applications. And we will present how this study extends to make feasible scheduling decision in order to meet the deadline on aperiodic and sporadic preemptive real-time systems in addition to fixed priority and periodic preemptive task set.
